newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt lets in Irish cows despite ban.
newsitem.headline: Egypt lets in Irish cows despite ban.

text.p: The Egyptian authorities let Irish cattle ships dock in Alexandria and Port Said on Thursday despite a ban imposed on live cattle imports from Ireland because of mad cow disease.

The Friesian Express came into Alexandria harbour and the Bison into Port Said, each with about 1,600 cows aboard, port and cattle trade sources said. A third ship, the Galloway Express, is expected in Alexandria later on Thursday.
Port officials in Alexandria said they let the cows in because they had no notification of the ban, which was signed on Monday. It is not clear when exactly it comes into effect.

The trade sources said the Egyptian authorities appeared to be obscuring the issue of timing to avoid a repetition of what happened last March, when Irish Prime Minister John Bruton appealed directly to President Hosni Mubarak on behalf of Irish cows stranded in the Mediterranean by an earlier ban.

The new ban is in response to an increase in the incidence of mad cow disease, or bovine spongiform encephalopathy, in Ireland in 1996. It also covers live cattle imports from Switzerland, France and Portugal.
